product_backlog.title: List Management
product_backlog.description: Users can create, view, and delete to-do lists with names.
acceptance_criteria: User can create a new list with a name
User can view all lists they have created
User can delete a list (and its associated tasks)

product_backlog.title: Task Management
product_backlog.description: Users can add, complete, and delete tasks within lists.
acceptance_criteria: User can add a task with text to a list
User can mark a task as complete/incomplete
User can delete a task from a list
Completed tasks are visually distinguished

product_backlog.title: Web UI Foundation
product_backlog.description: A working web interface that presents lists and tasks and allows interaction.
acceptance_criteria: Web UI loads and displays all lists
Web UI displays all tasks within a selected list
All user actions are reflected immediately in the UI
Completed/incomplete distinction is clear visually

product_backlog.title: Data Persistence & Architecture
product_backlog.description: Design and implement the backend architecture including data storage approach.
acceptance_criteria: Persistence approach is chosen and documented
Data model supports lists and tasks
Backend API/routes enable all required operations

product_backlog.title: Choose and Document Tech Stack & Persistence Approach
product_backlog.user_story: As a developer, I want to understand the chosen technology stack and persistence strategy, so that I can build the app consistently and others can understand the design decisions.
acceptance_criteria: README documents chosen language/framework
README explains why this stack was chosen
Persistence approach (in-memory, file, DB) is documented with rationale
Architecture diagram or high-level design is documented
Setup instructions are clear enough to clone and run
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Team has shared understanding of architecture before implementation begins

product_backlog.title: Implement Data Model for Lists and Tasks
product_backlog.user_story: As the system, I need a data model that represents lists (with names) and tasks (with text and completion status), so that the app can store and retrieve this data.
acceptance_criteria: List entity has id and name
Task entity has id, text, completion status, and belongs to a list
Create operations work for both lists and tasks
Data persists according to chosen strategy
Data model supports all required operations (read, update, delete)
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Core data layer is in place for all other features to build on

product_backlog.title: Implement Backend API Routes for List Operations
product_backlog.user_story: As a frontend, I need API routes to create, read, and delete lists, so that the UI can manage lists.
acceptance_criteria: POST /lists endpoint creates a new list with a name
GET /lists returns all lists
GET /lists/:id returns a specific list
DELETE /lists/:id deletes a list and its tasks
Errors are handled gracefully with appropriate HTTP status codes
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Frontend can interact with lists via API

product_backlog.title: Implement Backend API Routes for Task Operations
product_backlog.user_story: As a frontend, I need API routes to create, read, update, and delete tasks, so that the UI can manage tasks.
acceptance_criteria: POST /lists/:id/tasks creates a new task with text
GET /lists/:id/tasks returns all tasks in a list
PATCH /lists/:id/tasks/:taskId updates task completion status
DELETE /lists/:id/tasks/:taskId deletes a task
Errors are handled gracefully
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Frontend can interact with tasks via API

product_backlog.title: Implement Home/Lists View UI
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to see all my lists on the home page, so that I can choose which list to work with.
acceptance_criteria: Home page displays a list of all lists with their names
Each list is clickable to view its tasks
There is a button to create a new list
The UI is clean and easy to understand without documentation
Lists load from the backend API
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: User can discover and navigate between their lists

product_backlog.title: Implement Create List Form
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to create a new list by entering a name, so that I can organize my tasks into separate lists.
acceptance_criteria: Form accepts a list name
Form submits to backend via API
New list appears in the lists view after creation
User gets feedback (success/error) after submission
Form can be opened from the home page
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: User can create lists through the UI

product_backlog.title: Implement List Detail View with Tasks
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to view all tasks in a list, with clear visual distinction between completed and incomplete tasks, so that I can see what work remains.
acceptance_criteria: List detail page shows all tasks for the selected list
Incomplete tasks are displayed differently from complete ones (e.g., strikethrough or grayed out)
There is a button to add a new task
There is a button to delete the entire list
Back button returns to lists view
Tasks load from the backend API
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: User can see task status at a glance

product_backlog.title: Implement Add Task Form
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to add a new task to a list by typing a description, so that I can track what needs to be done.
acceptance_criteria: Form accepts task text
Form submits to backend via API
New task appears in the task list after creation
Task is marked as incomplete by default
User gets feedback (success/error) after submission
Form is accessible from the list detail view
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: User can create tasks through the UI

product_backlog.title: Implement Toggle Task Completion
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to click a task to mark it as complete or incomplete, so that I can track my progress.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a task toggles its completion status
The UI immediately reflects the change (visual distinction)
Completion status is persisted via backend API
User gets clear visual feedback on the new status
Toggle works without page reload
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: User can track task completion directly in the UI

product_backlog.title: Implement Delete Task Functionality
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to delete a task from a list, so that I can remove tasks I no longer need.
acceptance_criteria: Each task has a delete button or option
Clicking delete removes the task from the list
Deletion is confirmed via backend API
Task list updates immediately after deletion
No hard page refresh required

product_backlog.title: Implement Delete List Functionality
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to delete an entire list (and all its tasks), so that I can remove lists I no longer need.
acceptance_criteria: Delete list button is available in the list detail view
Deletion may request confirmation
All tasks in the list are deleted with the list
User is returned to the lists view
Deletion is confirmed via backend API
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: User can clean up unwanted lists and their tasks

product_backlog.title: End-to-End Integration Testing
product_backlog.user_story: As QA, I want to verify the complete user flow works (create list, add tasks, mark complete, delete tasks, delete list), so that the product is ready for delivery.
acceptance_criteria: Full user flow can be executed without errors
All features work together correctly
No console errors or crashes during normal use
Visual distinction between complete/incomplete tasks is clear
All data operations persist and display correctly
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Product is ready to deliver to users

The product vision for this entire evaluation, verbatim, is:

# Fixed Evaluation Scenario: To-Do List Web App

> **Do not edit this file to "make the eval easier" or to match whatever the team
> produced.** Its entire value is being byte-identical across runs, so results are
> comparable across Horseless Carriage versions over time. If the scenario itself
> needs to change, that's a deliberate decision with its own commit message
> explaining why — never a silent drift.

This is the fixed input fed verbatim to the agent team as the product vision for
every automated team-performance evaluation run (see `RELEASE.md` "Team performance
evaluation" and `agents/scrum_team/scripts/run_eval.py`). It is intentionally small
enough to be fully deliverable within a 5-sprint, small-budget run, while still
requiring real design decisions (state persistence, list vs. item modeling,
basic UI) that differentiate a good team performance from a mediocre one.

## Product Vision

Build a simple to-do list web application. A single user should be able to:

1. Create a new to-do list with a name.
2. Add a task to a list, with a short text description.
3. Mark a task as complete or incomplete.
4. Delete a task.
5. Delete an entire list (and its tasks).
6. See all their lists and, within a list, all its tasks, with completed tasks
   visually distinguished from incomplete ones.

## Constraints (deliberately narrow, to keep this deliverable in 5 sprints)

- **Single user, no authentication.** Do not build login/accounts — out of scope.
- **No persistence requirement beyond the current session/process is assumed** unless
  the team's own design calls for it — persistence approach (in-memory, file, or a
  simple embedded DB) is a legitimate design decision for the team to make and
  justify, not a hidden requirement.
- **A working web UI is required** — the deliverable is something a person could
  open in a browser and actually use, not just a backend API with no way to
  interact with it.
- **No specific language/framework is mandated.** The team should choose something
  it can deliver completely and correctly within budget, and should say why.

## Explicitly out of scope (do not let these creep in)

- Multiple users, sharing, or permissions.
- Due dates, reminders, priorities, tags, or sub-tasks.
- Mobile app, offline support, or real-time sync.
- Any deployment/hosting beyond running locally.

## What "done" looks like after 5 sprints

A person can clone the repo, follow the README, run the app, and actually create a
list, add a few tasks, mark one complete, delete one, and delete a list — end to
end, without reading any code first.
